name: Heatmaps and scroll depth
plain: A script logs where people click, move and scroll so a color map of attention is built.
meaning: Shows which parts of the page attract clicks, how far people scroll (in 25 percent steps often) and rage clicks. Usually aggregated, but raw events are tied to a visitor ID and can feed session replay.

web.api: click, mousemove, scroll listeners sent to analytics vendor

access.persistence: Aggregate data retention set by vendor (30 days to 13 months common)
access.revocation: Clear site data, browser privacy settings

limits.headline: Can log where you click, move and scroll on a page to draw attention maps
limits.user_action: Nothing. It happens as you use a page with a heatmap script
can: Record where you click, tap and move the pointer
Record how far down you scroll
Combine many visitors into a color map for the site owner
cannot: Run on pages without the script
See what you do on other sites or apps
Show your name unless the site links it to a login
Work if a tracker blocker stops the script

story.what_it_is: A script draws a color map of where people click, move and scroll on a page.

marketing.name: Clarity heatmaps
marketing.pitch: Microsoft says Clarity heatmaps show where visitors click and scroll, to help improve pages.

story.for_you: You never see it. As you move your mouse, click and scroll, a script logs it. The site owner later sees a red and blue picture of the page that shows which parts got attention.
story.for_makers: Design teams want to see why people do not click a button or never see a offer. Heatmaps show scroll depth and rage clicks. The same events often feed session replay, so they tie to a visitor ID.

use_cases.example: A store sees that most visitors never scroll to the Buy button and moves it up.
A browser game site sees where players click on its menu, and fixes the Play button that people miss.
A news site sees that readers stop at 40 percent of an article and puts the subscribe box earlier.
A software firm sees that people click a non-clickable image on the pricing page and makes it a link.
An advertiser sees which part of a landing page draws clicks, then rewrites the headline.
Rage clicks on a menu show that keyboard and screen reader users get stuck, and the team fixes it.

risks: Mouse paths show what you read

technical_bounds: Mouse movement is off on touch

history.change: Free heatmap tools such as Microsoft Clarity became common

refs.label: Freedom to Tinker session replay study
